newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end mostly flat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end mostly flat.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended mostly unchanged as players braced for $4.4 billion of new issues that they said should not depress prices provided they come at sensible levels like last week's deals.
"If you said 'Are they down marginally?,' maybe," one trader said of muni cash prices, adding that session was typical for a Monday. "There were some bid lists out after a very quiet morning."
A municipal analyst, however, judged prices flat to slightly higher. High-grade issues ended unchanged, while dollar bonds ended up a touch, he said. The analyst also cited bid lists.
The trader estimated that lists totaled $150 million. Accounts were apparently trying to lighten up ahead of the calendar, he said.

"If it's sort of like last week where the deals didn't get priced too far ahead of the market, they are reasonable, I think there is money there to buy them," he said. "I think it's strictly a function of what the underwriters decide to do."
This week's largest offering is a $709 million Puerto Rico deal expected Wednesday through Lehman Brothers. Fifty-one negotiated sales are expected totaling $2.9 billion.
Topping the competitive list is a $556 million Pennsylvania deal on Tuesday. Fifty-six competitive sales are expected totaling $1.5 billion.
Reid Smith, a senior portfolio manager and principal at Vanguard Group, said while he will look at Puerto Rico's deal, levels would have to be cheaper than usual for him to participate.

"I'm hestitant to buy Puerto Rico paper when I can buy insured paper within a specific state at cheaper levels," Smith said. "So I have not traditionally bought Puerto Rico, (and) we also are neutral at best in terms of long-term credit outlook."

The sale does, however, represents a large amount of supply that has trading value for investors looking for the dual tax exemption and for those in triple tax states like New York, he said. Puerto Rico paper is expect from local, state and federal taxes.
"(If) we can buy that close to the national levels or levels cheaper than what it historically trades at, then we are going to take a look at that," he said.
For 30-year paper, Smith would like to see the deal priced at five basis points through national levels to right on top of them, he said.
"It trades as much as 15 to 20 (basis points) through at times," Smith said.
Puerto Rico's deal aside, the portfolio manager said he isn't looking for anything in particular this week.

"I think we'll just look for opportunities where they fall," Smith said, adding that he may look at the $111 million North Carolina Medical Care Commission deal expected Wednesday via Merrill Lynch & Co.
"I tend to focus on some of the more unique specialty states that have good in-state demand," he said.
In debt futures, the June Municipal contract closed down 8/32 at 113-30/32. The June T-bond contract closed up 1/32 at 110-4/32. The MOB spread was 122 ticks.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 1/32 at 97-17/32 to yield 6.82 percent.
